problem: Prior surveys cover only one or two of vision, language and robotics, and focus on describing architectures rather than high-level challenges. No holistic analysis exists of embodied tasks that jointly use vision and language for planning in physical environments.
motivation: Embodied AI tasks combining vision and language (navigation, dialogue navigation, EQA, object referral, manipulation) are growing fast, but each subfield has its own conventions. A unifying view is needed to compare tasks and to identify what blocks generalisation and real-world deployment.
key_idea: Define Embodied Vision-Language Planning (EVLP) formally, organise the field into a taxonomy of tasks, approaches and evaluation, and identify core challenges for generalisation and real-world deployment.
insight: The paper is a position/survey piece with no experiments or ablations. Its main argument is that current EVLP work is limited by in-domain evaluation, simulator and dataset realism, and the lack of principled domain knowledge. It says future tasks should test cross-domain and cross-task generalisation, use dynamic environments, and measure intermediate behaviour rather than only task completion.
method: Problem definition: Formalises planning as Φ={S,A,s_ini,s_goal}, with states defined by vision-language input histories and a solution as an action sequence.

Task taxonomy: Groups tasks into VLN and vision-dialogue navigation, Embodied Question Answering, Embodied Object Referral, and Goal-directed Manipulation, distinguished by action space, reasoning mode and interaction with another agent.

Approaches and learning paradigms: Reviews modelling of vision, language, multimodal alignment/fusion and action planning, plus semi/self/fully-supervised learning, RL, pre-training, augmentation, multitask learning, reward shaping and cycle-consistency.
Evaluation review: Compares datasets, simulators, and metrics grouped as distance, success, path similarity, instruction-based and object-centric.

Core challenges: Covers new directions (social interaction, dynamic environments, cross-task learning, interactive perception), domain knowledge (pre-training, commonsense), training objectives, and the sim-to-real gap.
numbers_note: Survey extended abstract; no experimental results reported.
results: No empirical results. The contribution is a formal EVLP definition, a taxonomy, a survey of tasks, datasets, simulators and metrics, and a list of core challenges: generalisation, robustness, simulator and dataset realness, use of domain knowledge, and richer interaction.
limitations: Extended abstract with little depth; details are deferred to the JAIR journal article.
Purely qualitative and pre-LLM: no quantitative comparison of methods and no coverage of LLM/foundation-model agents.
builds_on: Francis et al. 2022 JAIR survey (Core challenges in embodied vision-language planning)
